children: According to ChainCatcher citing the Financial Times, RBC and Oxford Economics, the U.S. will release several economic reports next week, Nov. 23-27, with key data due Wednesday ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. October core PCE inflation, the Federal Reserve’s Beige Book and remarks by New York Fed President John C. Williams are among the indicators investors will watch for clues on December rate-hike expectations.

Markets sold off last week amid concerns about AI investment and inflation. The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell 8.02%, 8.61% and 10.02%, respectively; the S&P 500 and Dow entered correction territory, while the VIX briefly reached 40. Spot gold and silver dropped 8.84% and 15.39%, and the U.S. dollar index rose for a fourth consecutive week.

At 9:30 PM Wednesday, the U.S. is scheduled to release October core PCE, its revised annualized third-quarter GDP growth rate and initial jobless claims for the week ended Nov. 21. The market expects core PCE to rise to 3.2% year over year from 3.1%, and claims to come in at 197,000, down from 203,000. RBC forecasts monthly increases of 0.3% in both headline and core PCE, with annual rates reaching 3.8% and 3.3%. It said inflation is reaccelerating and flagged pressure from energy costs, lower savings and higher personal interest payments.

Williams is scheduled to speak at 5:00 AM Tuesday, and the Fed will publish its Beige Book at 3:00 AM Thursday. Minutes from the October meeting said almost all participants considered further rate increases potentially appropriate; some said a larger December increase could be considered if inflation data were unfavorable. The European Central Bank will release its October meeting minutes at 8:30 PM Thursday. U.S. weekly ADP employment data is also due Tuesday.

Investors will watch Black Friday spending for signs of household resilience to inflation, energy prices and borrowing costs. Oxford Economics forecasts holiday retail sales growth of 4.2% this year. Concerns over data-center financing needs and political resistance continue to weigh on AI stocks. The Financial Times reported that the Trump administration wants to reach a Ukraine ceasefire deal by Jan. 3 next year; European officials fear the push could pressure Ukraine into major concessions.
The Tokyo Stock Exchange will be closed Nov. 23, and the New York Stock Exchange will close Nov. 26 for Thanksgiving. Trading on Nov. 27 will end early at 2:00 AM on Nov. 28 (UTC+8).

title: U.S. October Core PCE and Fed Beige Book to Test Rate-Hike Expectations Before Thanksgiving
